title: the picture of the Emacs layer shows the bridge and the scopes of the answers, and the check follows every name of it
intent: The second picture of the catch-up plan D2: the Emacs layer (D3 of `docs/SITE-DIAGRAMS-PLAN.md' §8).  The section of the site that carries it (`*why-emacs*') is the most textual place of the site -- six points (BUFFERS, INTROSPECT, EDIT, DIAGNOSE, COMPOSE, RECOVER) and not one picture -- and it is the place where the bridge belongs: the bridge is the only path to the live state of the editor's Emacs, and that is the thought the section rests on, so it is written on the arrow itself.  The picture names the person, the editor's Emacs, the agent's Emacs and the bridge between them, the six capabilities of the layer, the five modules that hold the layer together -- `lib/yeah-emacs.el', `lib/yeah-bridge.el', `lib/yeah-compose.el', `lib/yeah-doctor-ui.el' and `lib/yeah-approval-ui.el' -- and one line that names the five answers the person may give: `:once', `:session', `:project', `:global' and `:reject'.  The claim of the wave is new (`the-emacs-layer-diagram-shows-the-bridge-and-the-scopes').
objection: The picture shows the layer as the code shows it.  (a) **The bridge on the picture is one bridge and the code has two names for a bridge**: `lib/yeah-bridge.el' is the way *from* the agent's Emacs *to* the live state of the editor's Emacs, and the socket over which the editor drives the service is a different thing (`lib/yeah-service.el', `lib/yeah-client.el') that belongs to the picture of the placements (D4); the arrow of the picture says so in words.  (b) **DIAGNOSE is one capability with two halves**: `lib/yeah-doctor-ui.el:148' is the doctor that the person runs in his own editor and `lib/yeah-emacs.el:152' is the diagnostics that the agent calls in its own Emacs; both links stand in one block, and two blocks with one name would look like a mistake to the reader of the site.  (c) **The six capabilities are the six of the site**: the check knows them by name, so a capability that the code gains and the picture does not is not caught here.  (d) **The picture is not on the site** -- that is the wave D3.
refuted_by: the picture names a file, a line or a definition that is not there, a block of the picture names no file, the picture has no block of the bridge or the block of the bridge names no file of `lib/yeah-bridge.el', the picture drops one of the five modules that hold the layer together, the picture has no line that names the five answers of the person, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The decisions of the parent (2026-11-22; a rule outside §17.2, the owner may cancel it): the name of the picture is `emacs-layer'; the bridge is named by the alias `bridge' and the check holds that alias to the block of the bridge, so the picture cannot move the bridge out of sight; the line with the five answers is the same word for word as in D1, as §4 of the catch-up plan asks.  The measurements of the writer: the check of the picture is green; four controls bite -- the reference of `lib/yeah-bridge.el:177' removed, the line of the five answers removed, the reference of `lib/yeah-bridge.el:210' removed, and the tree without the pictures refused with the code 2 -- and every one of them bites with its own assertion.  The finding that the writer named and that the package kept: **the first control did not bite**.  In the first version of the picture `lib/yeah-bridge.el' was named twice (in the block BUFFERS and in the block of the bridge), so the rule "the module is named somewhere" held even when the link of the bridge was removed, and the check answered 0.  The picture is now held by two rules -- every block names a file, and the block with the alias `bridge' names `lib/yeah-bridge.el' -- and the control bites.  A measured control is a result and not an intention: the first answer is in the report of the writer and not in the claim.
